Priya: Heads-up — saw a 90th pct decode latency spike on the staging cluster after yesterday's kernel mapping change. digging in.
Jorge: repro steps? which model, batch sizes, and was kv warm?
Priya: model=redwood-7b-q4, workload=chat_low_latency, peak batch formation shows many tiny decode batches (1-2) after big prefill batches. KV hit-rate dropped ~18% in same window.
Lina: that smells like handshake/queue release ordering. if prefill drains and then decode requests get scheduled onto a different kernel with cold kv, latency jumps.
Cam: can you paste the tracing snapshot? also ping the deploy bot for the kernel map that rolled.
Priya: trace snippet:
```
[12:03:11.482] prefill batch size=48 -> kernel=matmul_v2_fast
[12:03:11.511] prefill finish -> handshake notify
[12:03:11.512] decode req queued -> kernel selector -> smallbatch path -> kernel=matmul_v1
[12:03:11.513] kv lookup miss -> fetch -> +8ms
[12:03:11.521] decode start -> total latency 67ms (prev baseline 24ms)
```
Cam: aha — kernel divergence (matmul_v2_fast vs matmul_v1) plus tokenbudget forcing small decode batches. selector fallback looks too eager.
Jorge: here's the selector config that shipped:
```
selector:
  prefer_fast_kernel: true
  fallback_threshold_tokens: 16
  smallbatch_limit: 4
  kv_affinity_tolerance_ms: 5
```
Lina: kv_affinity_tolerance_ms=5 is too low for our warmup patterns. when kernels differ we should hold decode for a soft window to allow KV priming or prefer same-kernel decode routing.
Priya: experiment idea: introduce phase-aware delay for decode when preceding prefill batch used a different kernel. naive config:
```
if prefill.kernel != candidate.kernel:
  hold_decode_ms = min(10 + 0.5 * prefill.size, 50)
else:
  hold_decode_ms = 0
```
Cam: also try adjusting token budget heuristics — bump fallback_threshold_tokens to 32 and smallbatch_limit to 8 for a canary. That will reduce number of tiny decode batches.
Jorge: perf profiling: ran `./perf.sh --trace --slot 12 --model redwood-7b-q4 --workload chat_low_latency` — attaching result (summary):
- kernel switch overhead ~4.5ms
- kv miss penalty ~7-9ms
- additional scheduling jitter ~2-3ms
Priya: with soft hold (15ms) and selector tweaks, locally saw 90th pct drop from 67ms -> 28ms. KV hit-rate returned to baseline.
Lina: good. are there any downsides? increased p50? token cost? request queuing?
Priya: p50 unchanged, some requests saw +10ms tail in prefill-heavy mixes because of hold; overall 99th improved. cost impact negligible.
Cam: let's run a short canary: rollout selector tweak and phase-hold on 10% of traffic in staging for 2h. add logs for kernel affinity mismatches and kv hit-rate.
Priya: doing that now — enabling flags: `phase_hold=1, selector_override={fallback_threshold_tokens:32, smallbatch_limit:8}`. will report back.
DevBot: Deploy queued: canary rollout to staging (10%) scheduled at 2026-03-18T12:15:00Z. Link: https://ci.internal/deploy/7891 :rocket:
Jorge: if canary looks good, follow-up items:
- add metric `kernel_mismatch_count` and alert if >5% of requests
- consider persistent kernel affinity hints per session
- evaluate lowering kernel selection aggressiveness in mixed-quantization models
Priya: noted. I'll post results in ~2h. thanks all :thumbsup:
Cam: thanks, especially for clear trace. if it regresses after canary, revert selector flags and re-evaluate kv priming path.
Priya: update 2h later: canary looks good — 90th down across canary instances, kv hit-rate stable. promoting to 50% tomorrow morning for longer soak.
Lina: awesome. let's keep the phase-hold conservative and add telemetry dashboards. created a quick grafana panel: /d/redwood/prefill-decode-kv-affinity
Priya: saved notes to perf playbook and will open a follow-up RFC for persistent kernel affinity caching.
Cam: great work everyone.
